title: Madeline the mare?
html_source:
It has been suggested that these lines reference Madeleine Lemaire, a French painter famous for portraits and flowers.

The name Madeline is an English form of the name Magdalene. This is congruent with the multitude of Biblical references in Ulysses.

It is also interesting to note that mare is the Latin word for sea. Another common theme in Ulysses.

The sea also seams to represent a motherly figure. Further reinforcing the themes of the book. Mother Mary, the sea.

Also, mare might well be connected to nightmare. This builds on the dreams Daedalus has of his own deceased mother.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: mare: female horse
joycean pun?

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: A famous racing brood mare named Madeline was owned by American statesman Henry Clay
